summary: God commands the sanctuary to be erected and consecrated, and Moses assembles its structure and furnishings on the first day of the second year. When the work is finished, the cloud covers the tent and God's glory fills it so that Moses cannot enter; the cloud and nighttime fire then govern Israel's journeys.
whyItMatters: The book reaches its promised dwelling among the rescued people, yet divine presence remains more than even Moses can freely enter. The final scene prepares for a continuing life of worship and travel under visible guidance.

context.author: Exodus does not name its final author. It records Moses writing particular covenant material; traditional Mosaic attribution and modern accounts of composition are distinguished in the book briefing.
context.audience: Israel remembering its rescue from Egypt and its obligations as a covenant community. The chapter does not identify an individual dedicatee.
context.date: The narrative places these events at Sinai after the departure from Egypt. The date of the events and the history of the book’s composition are separate, debated questions.
context.setting: Israel's camp on the first day of the first month of the second year, followed by a closing description of the cloud throughout the journeys.
context.literaryForm: Instructions for erection and consecration, a matching fulfillment narrative, and a concluding manifestation and travel pattern.

before.text: All the manufactured parts and priestly garments have been brought to Moses, inspected, and blessed. They are now ready to become the assembled and functioning sanctuary.

here.text: The command and execution proceed from the inner furnishings to the court, after which divine glory occupies the completed tent and the cloud governs movement.

after.text: Exodus ends with God present in the completed tent and directing the journeys. Leviticus opens with God calling to Moses from the Tent of Meeting (Leviticus 1:1), continuing the question of how the people will live and worship around this presence.

outline.heading: The date and order of assembly
outline.note: The furnishings and court are assigned their places.

outline.heading: Consecration of objects and priests
outline.note: Oil, washing, and garments set apart the dwelling and its ministers.

outline.heading: The structure and ark erected
outline.note: Moses follows the command at the stated date and screens the covenant ark.

outline.heading: Table, lamps, incense, and entrance
outline.note: The inner space is arranged and its service begun.

outline.heading: Outer altar, washing, and court completed
outline.note: Offerings, water, and the surrounding enclosure complete the work.

outline.heading: Glory and guidance
outline.note: The filled tent excludes Moses at this moment, and the cloud directs Israel’s travel and stopping.

keyVerses.text: In the first month in the second year, on the first day of the month, the tabernacle was raised up.
keyVerses.why: The erection receives a precise place in the book’s own calendar.

keyVerses.text: Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and Yahweh’s glory filled the tabernacle.
keyVerses.why: The completed dwelling becomes the site of the divine presence anticipated through the instructions.

keyVerses.text: For the cloud of Yahweh was on the tabernacle by day, and there was fire in the cloud by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys.
keyVerses.why: The final verse extends the visible cloud and fire into the people’s continuing journeys.

questions.question: When is the tabernacle erected?
questions.answer: The command specifies the first day of the first month, and the fulfillment identifies it as the second year. The book thereby dates the erection within its own departure-and-wilderness chronology, without naming a modern calendar year.

questions.question: Why does the assembly begin with the ark and veil?
questions.answer: The initial instructions place the covenant ark within the tent and screen it, then arrange the table, light, incense altar, and outer objects around that interior. The execution follows the same movement from the protected center toward the court.

questions.question: What does “sanctify” mean in the instructions?
questions.answer: It means set apart the objects and priests for their assigned holy service. Oil is applied to the dwelling and furnishings, while the priests are washed, clothed, and anointed for ministry.

questions.question: Is the completed sanctuary left as an unused display?
questions.answer: Moses sets out the bread, lights the lamps, burns incense, and presents offerings; water is also supplied for washing. The report describes the equipment entering service as it is placed.

questions.question: Who uses the basin in this chapter?
questions.answer: Moses, Aaron, and Aaron's sons wash their hands and feet there before entering the tent or approaching the altar. The fulfillment report names Moses alongside the priestly family, a detail easily missed when reading only the earlier instructions.

questions.question: Why can Moses not enter after finishing the work?
questions.answer: The cloud settles on the tent and God's glory fills it, preventing his entry at this moment. Completion has brought the promised presence, but it does not make that presence subject to unrestricted human access.

questions.question: How do the people know when to travel?
questions.answer: They move when the cloud lifts and remain where they are when it does not. The closing description places the cloud by day and fire by night in the sight of the whole household of Israel throughout its journeys.

glossary.def: Set apart a person or object for the holy service assigned in the instructions.
The covenant material Moses places inside the ark before screening it with the veil.
The manifestation of God that fills the tent and prevents Moses from entering at its completion.
